content: Be less curious about people and more curious about ideas.
author: Marie Curie
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

Across his life and work, Marie Curie saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
